items.criterion: A corpus that names a test obligation in a non-git directory with no --repo-root still refuses rc 2 unresolvable-repo-root (AUG-127 invariant measured at the CLI, not only via pytest).
items.detail: Built /var/tmp/hermes-scratch/tmp.MCzFAvshvw/specs/contract.xml (non-git dir) naming runner=pytest path=tests/test_xml_specs.py. `spec validate specs` and `spec check specs` both -> rc 2, "spec error (invalid-spec-graph): unresolvable-repo-root: /var/tmp/hermes-scratch/tmp.MCzFAvshvw/specs is not inside a git work tree and no --repo-root was given; pass --repo-root <repository> ...". Matches auger.py:13409-13412.

items.criterion: An explicit --repo-root is still validated eagerly even for an obligation-free corpus (a bad explicit root is a typed refusal, not silently ignored).
items.detail: Copied examples/xml/minimal.xml into a non-git dir and ran `spec validate <dir> --repo-root <nonexistent>` -> rc 2, "spec error (invalid-spec-graph): unresolvable-repo-root: .../nope is not a directory; --repo-root must name the repository ...". Code: auger.py:13297-13301 calls _spec_repository_root eagerly whenever repository_root is not None. Also pinned by tests/test_spec_repository_root.py:427-432.

items.criterion: The lazy resolution is not a fallback to auger's own tree: a corpus naming a test that exists only in auger's checkout is still refused outside a repo.
items.detail: My CLI run above named tests/test_xml_specs.py (exists and is tracked in auger) from a non-git dir and got rc 2 unresolvable-repo-root — no fallback to auger's tree. Pinned by tests/test_spec_repository_root.py:347 test_no_root_and_no_flag_refuses_instead_of_using_augers_tree and :178 test_the_checked_file_is_the_consumers_copy_not_augers, both in the 9-passed run.

items.criterion: The lazy root is resolved from the SPEC ROOT, so a corpus inside a git repo still resolves obligations against that repo's top level.
items.detail: auger.py:13412 calls _spec_repository_root(root, None) where root is the spec root, and auger.py:13135 does _git_toplevel(Path(spec_root)). tests/test_spec_repository_root.py:138 runs `validate <repo>/specs` with no flag inside a throwaway git repo -> rc 0 + "spec: 1 document(s), 2 block(s), 1 reference(s) ok"; :178 proves the file read is the consumer's copy, not auger's. Both passed in the 9-passed run.

items.criterion: The docs' installed-layout example command still works as written and the schema doc's lazy-root paragraph matches the code's actual behaviour.
items.detail: docs/XML-SPEC-SCHEMA.md:52 shape reproduced on this tree: `auger.py spec validate examples/xml --repo-root $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` -> "spec: 1 document(s), 2 block(s), 1 reference(s) ok" rc 0 (also rc 0 without the flag). The paragraph at :100-108 (explicit eager / implicit lazy at first path-migration-fixture / step-3 refusal unchanged) matches auger.py:13297-13309 and 13409-13412 exactly.
